*Li-awwali al-hashr* (﴿At the first gathering﴾): That is, it was the first gathering and the second gathering, which was from Khaybar to al-Sham.

*Ma zanantum an yakhrujU* (﴿You did not think that they would depart﴾): That is, you did not think, O believers, that Banu al-Nadir would leave their homes.

*Wa zannu annahum mani'atuhum husunuhum mina Allah* (﴿And they thought their fortresses would protect them from Allah﴾): That is, the Jews of Banu al-Nadir thought that their fortresses would prevent them from what Allah had decreed against them, namely their expulsion from al-Madina.

*Fa-atahumu Allahu min haythu lam yahtasibu* (﴿So Allah came to them from where they had not expected﴾): That is, Allah came to them from where they had not imagined they would be reached.

*Wa qadhafa fi qulubihimu ar-ru'b* (﴿And He cast terror into their hearts﴾): That is, Allah the Exalted cast intense fear of Muhammad and his companions into them.

*Yukhribuna buyutahum bi-aydihim* (﴿They destroyed their houses by their own hands﴾): That is, they destroyed their houses so that the believers could not benefit from them, and so that they could take with them some of their doors and their attractive timber.

*Wa aydi al-mu'minin* (﴿And by the hands of the believers﴾): Since the believers were demolishing the fortifications over them, so that they could fight them.

*Fa'tabiru ya ulil-absar* (﴿So take warning, O people of insight﴾): That is, learn a lesson from their condition, O people of intellect, and do not be deceived, and do not rely on anything except Allah, glorified and exalted be He.

*Wa lawla an kataba Allahu 'alayhimu al-jala'* (﴿And had Allah not decreed for them exile﴾): That is, had Allah not decreed for them departure from al-Madina.

*La'adhdhabahum fi ad-dunya* (﴿He would have punished them in this world﴾): That is, by killing and taking captive, just as He punished their brothers Banu Qurayza with that.

Allah the Exalted informs of His majesty and greatness: that He is glorified, that is, declared free of every deficiency, whether associate, consort, offspring, incapacity or imperfection, absolutely, by the tongue of speech and the tongue of state, by everything in the heavens and on the earth: the angels, humans, jinn, animals, trees, stones and clods of earth. This happened because He cast into their hearts terror and intense fear of the Messenger and his companions, so that they came to destroy their own houses with their own hands and the hands of the believers.

This is because the treaty concluded between them and the Messenger and the believers stipulated that they would carry their wealth, except for the weapons (*al-halqah*, meaning armour), and depart from the land to al-Sham, which was their first gathering. So whenever a door or a piece of timber pleased them, they would pull it from its place, and the house would be ruined as a result.

Learn a lesson from the condition of the strong Banu al-Nadir: how Allah cast terror into their hearts and they were expelled from their homes. Whoever opposes Allah, Allah will punish him with the most severe punishments, for Allah is severe in punishment.

That was by the permission of Allah, so there is no sin upon you for it. By it He gladdened the believers and disgraced the defiantly disobedient Jews.

1. The demonstration of Allah's majesty and greatness, together with His might and wisdom, in His being glorified by all creatures above and below, and in the expulsion of Banu al-Nadir from their homes. This was the first gathering, and it was accomplished for them, and a second and third gathering will follow it.

They had strength, and the believers were weak, yet they were routed with the worst defeat, abandoned the land and wealth, and departed never to return. Those who take heed learn from such things, for no strength avails against the strength of Allah. 4. The pardon of Allah for the mujtahid (one who exerts independent judgment) when he errs, and His not holding him to account. The believers exerted their judgment in cutting the palm trees of Banu al-Nadir in order to enrage them until they came down from their fortresses. They erred in this, for cutting down fruit-bearing palms is corruption, but Allah the Exalted did not hold them to account, because they were mujtahids.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 59, verse 6–7:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Wa-ma afa'a Allahu 'ala rasulihi minhum﴾: That is, what God returned into the hand of the Messenger of God ﷺ from the property of the Banu al-Nadir.

﴿Fa-ma awjaftum 'alayhi min khaylin wa-la rikab﴾: That is, you did not hasten in seeking it and obtaining it with horses or camels; that is, you did not undergo hardship in it.

﴿Wa-lakinna Allaha yusallitu rusulahu 'ala man yasha'﴾: That is, God has given His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ power over the Banu al-Nadir, and their lands were opened by peace treaty.

﴿Wa-ma afa'a Allahu 'ala rasulihi min ahli al-qura﴾: That is, what God returned to His Messenger from the property of the people of the towns, over which no horses or riders were driven.

﴿Fa-lillahi wa-lilrasuli wa-li-dhi al-qurba wa-al-yatama wa-al-masakin wa-ibn al-sabil﴾: That is, there is a share for God, a share for the Messenger, a share for the relatives of the Messenger, a share for the orphans, a share for the needy and a share for the wayfarer; it is distributed equally among those mentioned.

﴿Kay la yakuna dulatan bayna al-aghniya' minkum﴾: That is, so that wealth does not circulate only among the strong rich, and the weak and poor do not receive it.

﴿Wa-ma atakumu al-rasulu fa-khudhuhu wa-ma nahakum 'anhu fa-intahu﴾: That is, whatever the Messenger gave you and permitted you, or commanded you, take it; and whatever he forbade you and prohibited you from, and did not permit you, refrain from it.

﴿Wa-ittaqu Allaha inna Allaha shadid al-'iqab﴾: That is, fear God by not disobeying Him or His Messenger, and beware of God's punishment for disobeying Him and His Messenger, for God is severe in punishment.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues on the expedition against the Banu al-Nadir, after the peace that was concluded between them and the Messenger of God ﷺ, when they left their orchards (hawa'it, i.e. their gardens) as spoils (fay') for the Messenger of God ﷺ. The Muslims desired those gardens, and some of them thought they would be divided among them as booty is divided. God Most High refused this for them and said: ﴿And what God gave as spoil to His Messenger﴾, that is, what God Most High returned to His Messenger of the property of the Banu al-Nadir. The word "returned" (radd) is an explanation of the word "afa'a," because fay' (spoil) is the shadow that shrinks and then returns, that is, is returned. The property of the Banu al-Nadir originally belongs to the Messenger of God ﷺ, because the Banu al-Nadir had made a covenant with the Messenger of God, and by the terms of the covenant he left them their property. When they broke the covenant and betrayed it, they deserved nothing of the wealth, especially since they conspired to kill him and nearly carried out their crime, the consequences of which they bore. Even had they not carried it out. The beginning of the matter is as follows:

Among the clauses of the covenant concluded between the Messenger ﷺ and the Banu al-Nadir was that they would contribute with the Messenger to the blood-money (diyat) that might be incurred. About six months after the Battle of Uhud, it happened that 'Amr ibn Umayya al-Damri killed two men from the Banu Kalb, or Banu Kilab, by mistake. Their kinsmen came demanding their blood-money from the Messenger of God ﷺ, since he was responsible for the Muslims. He ﷺ went out to the Banu al-Nadir in their village, which lies two miles from Medina, seeking their contribution to the blood-money of the two Kalbis, according to the covenant. When he reached them, they seated him and his companions in the best place and said: "Whatever you ask, it is yours, O Abu al-Qasim." Then they withdrew among themselves and said: "The opportunity is at hand to be rid of the man." They brought a millstone ("rahan," a mill) of rock and went up with it to the roof of the house, intending to drop it on the head of the Messenger of God ﷺ while he sat in the shade of the wall with his companions. Before they dropped the millstone, God revealed to His Messenger that he should rise from his place, for the Jews intended to drop a stone on him to kill him. He ﷺ rose immediately and his companions followed him, and the plot fell into the hands of the Jews.

As soon as the Messenger ﷺ returned, he announced the march against the Banu al-Nadir, for they had broken their covenant and fighting them became obligatory. He encamped in their courtyard and besieged them. An embassy took place and ended in a settlement stipulating that the Banu al-Nadir would leave Medina, carrying their property on their camels but not their weapons, and would join Adhriʿat in Syria. This was the first gathering of them to the land of the return (ard al-ma'ad) and the place of assembly, except for two households who settled in Khaybar, the family of the Banu al-Huqayq, among whom was Huyayy ibn Akhtab, father of Safiyya, wife of the Messenger of God ﷺ. This expedition has a sequel that will come at His saying ﴿Have you not seen those who played the hypocrite, saying to their brothers among the People of the Book who disbelieved...﴾ [al-Hashr: 11] and the verses that follow.

From here we learn that the property of the Banu al-Nadir belongs to the Messenger of God ﷺ, which God gave him as spoil; so He said: ﴿And what God gave as spoil to His Messenger from them﴾, that is, from the Banu al-Nadir. When the believers coveted it, God Most High said in response to them: ﴿You did not spur any horse or camel against it﴾, that is, against the property of the Banu al-Nadir; you did not ride toward it on horses or camels, nor did you hasten on foot toward them, because they were at the edge of Medina, so you bore no journey, no fatigue, and no fighting unto death or wounds; therefore you have no claim to it, for it is spoil and not booty. But God gives His messengers power over whom He wills, without war or fighting, so He grants them spoil from the wealth of the disbelievers, which is God's wealth, and He returns it to His messengers. God, according to His custom with His messengers, gave Muhammad ﷺ power over his enemies, the Banu al-Nadir, so he obtained the wealth without fighting or travel, and it is his alone, to spend as he wills; yet he spent it, and nothing remained of it except the provision for one year for his wives, may God be pleased with them and make them pleased. God's saying ﴿And God is over all things competent﴾ means that no strong one can resist Him, and no noble or mighty one can overpower Him.

His saying Most High: ﴿What God gave as spoil to His Messenger from the people of the towns﴾, that is, from the property of the people of the towns that were not conquered by force but by peace treaty. That wealth is distributed as spoil in the manner God has stated: ﴿for God and for the Messenger and for the near relatives﴾, that is, the relatives of the Messenger ﷺ, namely the Banu Hashim and the Banu al-Muttalib.

﴿And the orphans﴾, who have no provider; ﴿and the needy﴾, whom need has reduced to poverty; ﴿and the wayfarer﴾, who is the traveler cut off from his country, home and property. The reason for this God explained in His saying: ﴿So that it does not become a circulating commodity﴾, that is, the wealth should not circulate ﴿among the rich among you﴾, and the weak and the poor should not receive it. Thus it is out of mercy and justice that the spoil is distributed among these mentioned categories. What belongs to God is spent on public welfare, and likewise what belongs to the Messenger after his death ﷺ; the remainder goes to those mentioned. Similarly, one-fifth of the booty is distributed among those mentioned in this verse, while the four-fifths go to the warriors.

His saying Most High: ﴿And what the Messenger gave you﴾ of wealth or otherwise, ﴿take it, and what he forbade you﴾, that is, of wealth or otherwise, ﴿refrain from it, and fear God; do not disobey Him or His Messenger, and beware of His punishment, for God is severe in punishment,﴾ that is, His punishment is harsh and severe, unbearable; so woe to whoever confronts it with disbelief, depravity and wrongdoing.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Clarification that the property of the Banu al-Nadir was spoil specifically belonging to the Messenger of God ﷺ.

2- That spoil (fay'), which is what the Muslims obtain without fighting, but rather through the flight of the enemy and his abandonment of it, or through a peace concluded between him and the Muslims, is distributed as mentioned in this verse: ﴿What God gave as spoil to His Messenger from the people of the towns belongs to God, and to the Messenger, and to the near relatives, and the orphans, and the needy, and the wayfarer.﴾ As for booty (ghanima), which is what is taken by force and to which the Muslims travelled, one-fifth is set aside for God, the Messenger, the near relatives, the orphans, the needy and the wayfarer, distributed among them equally, and the remaining four-fifths are divided among the fighters who took part in the battles and engaged in them: a share for the foot soldier and two shares for the horseman.

3- The obligation to obey the Messenger of God ﷺ, to apply his rulings, to follow his confirmed practice (sunna), and the prohibition of opposing him in what he forbade his community. The two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) narrated that Ibn Mas'ud (may God be pleased with him) said: "God curses the tattooers and those who have themselves tattooed, those who pluck facial hair, and those who file teeth for beauty, who alter God's creation." This reached a woman of the Banu Asad called Umm Ya'qub, who used to recite the Qur'an, and she said: "I have heard that you cursed such-and-such." He said: "Why should I not curse one whom the Messenger of God ﷺ cursed, and who is in the Book of God, mighty and majestic?" She said: "I have read everything between the two covers of the Mushaf and did not find it." He said: "If you had read it, you would have found it. Have you not read His saying: ﴿And what the Messenger gave you, take it; and what he forbade you, refrain from it﴾?" She said: "Yes." He said: "Indeed he ﷺ forbade it." That is, the tattooing, etc.

Explanation of the words:

﴿They tasted the evil consequence of their affair, and theirs is a painful punishment﴾: that is, they tasted the outcome of their disbelief and their war against the Messenger of Allah, and for them is a painful punishment in the Hereafter.

﴿Like the Shaytan when he says to man﴾: that is, and their likeness also in listening to the hypocrites and forsaking them is like the likeness of the Shaytan when he said to man:

﴿"Disbelieve." But when he disbelieves, he says, "Indeed, I am free of you."﴾: that is, Shaytan said to him, after having made him disbelieve, "Indeed, I am free of you."

﴿And that is the recompense of the wrongdoers﴾: that is, their abiding in the Fire, the one who goes astray and the one who is led astray; that is the recompense of them both and of the wrongdoers.

﴿And let a soul look to what it has put forward for tomorrow﴾: that is, let every person look at what he has sent forward for the Day of Resurrection, of good and evil.

﴿And do not be like those who forgot Allah﴾: that is, and do not be, O believers, like those who forgot Allah and so abandoned His obedience.

﴿So He caused them to forget themselves﴾: that is, He punished them by causing them to forget themselves, so they did no good deed at all.

﴿The companions of the Fire and the companions of Paradise are not equal﴾: because the companions of Paradise are the successful, safe from what is feared and triumphant in attaining what is desired and beloved, while the companions of the Fire are the losers.

﴿The companions of Paradise, they are the attainers of success﴾, ﴿abiding therein forever﴾. How, then, could the two be equal?

The Almighty said: ﴿Like those before them﴾. These verses [15], and the two after it [16] and [17], continue the discussion of Banu al-Nadir, where the Almighty said that the defeat of Banu al-Nadir after breaking their covenant is like that of those before them in time and place, namely Banu Qaynuqa', who broke their covenant, so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) expelled them. ﴿They tasted the evil consequence of their affair﴾, that is, the outcome of their breaking of the covenant and their disbelief in this world, ﴿and for them in the Hereafter is a painful punishment﴾, that is, a severe, agonizing torment. From the guidance of these verses:

1- Explanation of what the Qur'an contains of admonitions and lessons, command and prohibition, promise and warning, a matter which, if a mountain had been endowed with perception and discernment like a human and the Qur'an had been sent down upon it, it would have humbled itself and split out of fear of God.

2- Commendation of the striking of parables for alerting, teaching and guiding.

3- Affirmation of monotheism, that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God.

4- Affirmation of God's names, that they are all most beautiful, and that they contain sublime attributes.

5- Mention of His names is instruction for His servants to call upon Him by them and to seek nearness to Him through them.

As for His saying ﴿Glory be to God above what they associate﴾, He exalted Himself above what the polytheists associate with Him of idol-worshippers and others, and above everything worshipped besides Him, glorified and exalted is He. ﴿He is God, the Creator, the Originator, the Fashioner﴾: the One who measures creation; ﴿the Originator﴾, who brings it into being; ﴿the Fashioner﴾, who shapes it in the form He willed for it to be brought into existence. ﴿To Him belong the most beautiful names﴾, and they are one hundred names less one, as the Messenger of God ﷺ informed in Sahih al-Bukhari; His names contain His attributes, all His names are most beautiful and all His attributes are sublime, far above the attributes of created beings. ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Him﴾, that is, of created beings and existing things, He is exalted and sanctified above what does not befit Him, and they call upon Him and turn to Him for their continuance and the perfection of their life. ﴿And He is the Mighty, the Wise﴾, the Mighty who overcomes His affair, the Wise in the management of His dominion.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Explanation of what the Qur'an contains of admonitions and lessons, command and prohibition, promise and warning, a matter which, if a mountain had been endowed with perception and discernment like a human and the Qur'an had been sent down upon it, it would have humbled itself and split out of fear of God.

2- Commendation of the striking of parables for alerting, teaching and guiding.

3- Affirmation of monotheism, that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God.

4- Affirmation of God's names, that they are all most beautiful, and that they contain sublime attributes.

5- Mention of His names is instruction for His servants to call upon Him by them and to seek nearness to Him through them.
